technology.summary: Today's technology news includes a former Plaud executive raising $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background, Microsoft announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, and Amazon's use of over 1 million robot workers. Additionally, Fitbit has officially launched the Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker, and Apple is expected to make several smart home-related announcements at its upcoming "Welcome Home" event.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has teamed up with the Reserve Bank of India to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. However, global uncertainty has impacted the market and investor sentiment remains cautious, with benchmark indices facing a decline. Indian equity benchmarks have also experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence, as well as the Supreme Court's decision to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai were detained, while Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC for his ability to execute illegal orders. Former US President Donald Trump has called the US electoral process 'corrupt' in reference to an Indian election that did not happen.
